attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter essay, written in his own voice.

semantics.note: 'Only have so long before the markets sour' is firm language with no deadline. 'Will eventually' is a fair rendering. The antecedent (adoption slows or demand never arrives) is kept.

contract.note: The plain reading is ordinary: a broad AI-demand shortfall, then investors turning on all three firms because revenue does not justify capex. It is not stretched either way. The result depends on how the vague antecedent is read.

evidence.note: Microsoft's own disclosure (Q4 FY2026) that Azure demand exceeds capacity. It weighs against the antecedent, not the outcome, and it is a company statement covering one firm.
Census survey (Dec 2025 to May 2026): US business AI use roughly flat in many sectors but rising at larger firms. This does not establish a broad demand shortfall.
Reuters (Feb 2026): investors balked at Amazon's capex and punished Microsoft, but Google got a pass and demand was described as strong. The worry was about spending, not a demand failure.

reviews.rationale: This is a conditional forecast with no deadline. The packet does not establish the antecedent, a broad AI-demand slowdown or failure. Microsoft and Amazon report demand above capacity, and the Census data are mixed. Investor pushback in Feb 2026 targeted capex, not missing demand, and did not cover Google. With the antecedent unestablished, the claim cannot be scored.
